react_result.final_narrative_text: The treatment vs. control differential set is dominated by arachidonic acid and its downstream eicosanoid products, producing a striking cross-paradigm consensus across ORA (RaMP, MetaboAnalystR) and m/z-direct (Mummichog) analysis. Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) is the single highest-ranking pathway by RaMP ORA (FDR = 9.71e-14, fold enrichment = 1429.7) with five of nine input metabolites mapping to it. The same five driver metabolites — arachidonic acid (C00219), 15-HETE (C04742), 5-HETE (C04805), leukotriene A4 (C00909), and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 (C14717) — independently rank Arachidonic acid metabolism (KEGG:hsa00590) as the top KEGG entry by MetaboAnalystR PSEA and constitute a perfect 13-of-13 compound match to the Mummichog Arachidonic acid metabolism network module (p = 0.00084). Leukotriene metabolism (MUMM:leukotriene_metabolism, rank 3, p = 0.034) adds Leukotriene A4 as a second-generation eicosanoid driver, while Glycerophospholipid metabolism (MUMM:rank 1, p = 0.0096) connects glycerol (C00116) to the broader lipid signalling pool. The non-lipid metabolites (N-acetylgalactosamine, 2-ketobutyric acid, 4-hydroxybenzoic acid) contribute no hits to the eicosanoid cluster and appear as isolated peripheral signals. The biological interpretation is that the treatment strongly perturbs the cyclooxygenase and lipoxygenase branches of arachidonic acid metabolism, leading to coordinated elevation of HETEs, prostaglandin derivatives, and leukotrienes — a pattern consistent with inflammatory activation or phospholipase A2 stimulation.

react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolites converge on the Eicosanoid synthesis pathway (WP:WP167), confirmed across multiple enrichment paradigms. Arachidonic acid serves as the central substrate metabolized via cyclooxygenase (COX) and lipoxygenase (LOX) enzymes into pro-inflammatory lipid mediators. The five driver metabolites — 15-HETE, 5-HETE, 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2, and Leukotriene A4 — are all canonical eicosanoid intermediates detected with directional consistency in the treatment group. Glycerol, N-acetylgalactosamine, 2-ketobutyric acid, and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid do not associate with the eicosanoid network and appear as background signals. Cross-paradigm consensus on Eicosanoid synthesis provides strong biological evidence for a functional lipid-mediator shift under the treatment condition.
